comparison: Both strongly support the novelty claim (C2, C77) that this is the first termite pheromone receptor identification. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED and peer reviewers unanimously emphasize this as a major contribution advancing the field.

Both support PsimOR14's narrow tuning to neocembrene (C4, C42, C46, C51). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of SSR experiments with controls and dose-response data. Peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling' and 'convincing' for narrow tuning and neocembrene identification.

Both support narrow tuning claims (C5, C49, C50). OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive ligand screening (67 compounds) and sparseness metric (0.88). Peer reviewers confirm the narrow tuning is convincingly demonstrated using a large odorant set in the Drosophila empty neuron system.

Perfect agreement on native termite SSR data (C52-C57). Both evaluations support the identification of the specific sensillum expressing PsimOR14. OpenEval notes the correlation with heterologous expression validates the approach. Peer reviewers emphasize this allows anatomical localization of receptor expression on the antenna.

Both support caste-biased expression findings (C6, C75). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate replication and dual methodology (transcriptomics and electrophysiology). Peer reviewers confirm higher PsimOR14 expression in workers versus soldiers without questioning the finding.

Both support the correlation between expression and physiological sensitivity (C7, C76). OpenEval notes the correlation strengthens conclusions. Peer reviewers accept that higher worker expression corresponds well with stronger antennal responses, with all three reviewers confirming this relationship.

Perfect agreement on genomic and structural characterization (C58-C64). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on genome mapping and bioinformatic predictions. Peer reviewers accept the structural analysis as part of comprehensive characterization, though they note it supports rather than drives the main conclusions.

Both support computational docking results (C65-C68, C92). OpenEval notes correlation with experimental data provides validation while acknowledging inherent limitations. Peer reviewers accept the modeling as part of comprehensive characterization but explicitly state they lack expertise to evaluate technical quality.

Both support MD simulation findings (C73, C74). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while noting mechanistic significance remains speculative. Peer reviewers acknowledge this structural analysis but cannot technically evaluate it due to lack of expertise; they accept it as part of the overall characterization without challenge.

Both support phylogenetic analysis (C35-C37). OpenEval emphasizes the highly orthologous pattern across five termite species. Peer reviewers accept the phylogenetic approach as sound methodology for receptor selection and note it as part of the powerful integrated analysis.

Both support heterologous expression approach (C39-C41). OpenEval groups these with broader SSR experiments showing PsimOR14's selective response. Peer reviewers note the empty neuron system was used effectively, with negative/weak results for other ORs highlighting PsimOR14's specificity.

Both support dose-response characterization (C47, C48). OpenEval includes this as part of comprehensive SSR evidence. Peer reviewers note good sample size and that all parts build on each other, contributing to the 'compelling' evidence for narrow tuning.

Both support the inference that ORs mediate trail-following (C78). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting it's a reasonable inference from identifying PsimOR14 as neocembrene receptor, though technically inference rather than direct proof. Peer reviewers accept this as a logical conclusion contributing to understanding of termite chemoreception.

Both support validation of heterologous expression methodology (C84). OpenEval emphasizes the successful pheromone receptor identification confirms system suitability. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize this as a methodological contribution providing a framework for future termite OR studies.

OpenEval rates MM/PBSA results (C69-C70) as UNCERTAIN due to partial disagreement with experimental data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers acknowledged lack of expertise in computational modeling and did not specifically evaluate binding affinity calculations.

OpenEval rates PsimOR15 speculation (C106-C108) as UNCERTAIN, noting no functional characterization was performed despite reasonable speculation based on sequence similarity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates adaptive significance claims (C96-C99) as UNCERTAIN, noting caste-biased patterns are well-documented but adaptive significance is inferred rather than demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports extensive literature-based background (C1, C8-C23, C26-C34) as well-supported by appropriate citations establishing context. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background claims, focusing instead on novel empirical findings.

OpenEval rates speculation about shared receptors across termite species (C43, C79-C81) as UNCERTAIN, noting it remains a hypothesis requiring direct testing. Peer review R13 addresses C79 but not the broader speculation about shared receptors.

OpenEval supports contextualization of PsimOR14 tuning within pheromone receptor biology (C85-C87). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted narrow tuning without separately evaluating its placement in broader receptor biology context.
OpenEval rates speculation about geranylgeraniol and linalool effects (C88-C90) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but unsupported hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports evolutionary context claims (C100-C104) with appropriate citations, though notes some speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers focused on empirical findings rather than evolutionary interpretation.

OpenEval supports future research directions (C109-C113) as reasonable inferences from current findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate proposed future work.
